items.title: Types of Data: Structured and Unstructured

source_refs.note: 'Types of Data: Structured and Unstructured' under topic 6.2, as printed (PDF 77, printed 73).

blocks.text: Structured data is organized in a clear format, such as tables or spreadsheets. It has rows and columns that are easy to understand. Examples include students' mark sheets and databases. Unstructured data does not follow a fixed format (as shown in Figure 6.2). Examples include emails, images, audio, and videos. Unstructured data is difficult to analyze directly. Special tools are needed to process it. Both types of data are important. Modern systems use both structured and unstructured data.

blocks.alt: Two panels joined by a VS badge. Left, Structured Data: a table with columns ID, Name and Age and rows 1 Basim 16, 2 Umer 12, 3 Anie 15, and a ticked list: Tables, Databases, Spreadsheets. Right, Unstructured Data: icons of a picture, a text document, a chat bubble and a small app icon, and a list: Text, Images, Audio.
blocks.caption: Figure 6.2: Types of Data (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 6.2)
blocks.long_description: Structured data is shown as a neat table of rows and columns; unstructured data is shown as a mix of pictures, documents and messages.
